notes:
Account background: Copperleaf is a B2B fintech providing automated portfolio governance to institutional asset managers. They operate globally but need North America first-phase residency for customer datasets. They are procurement-led; primary concerns are data residency, vendor risk intake, and KMS ownership model.

Security & vendor intake status:
- InfoSec requested completed SIG/CAIQ and mapping to our shared responsibility matrix; they've sent their vendor questionnaire (30+ items) and want explicit answers for 'where does raw data live' and 'who controls encryption keys'.
- They require SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 copies (we have SOC2 in Drive link).
- Audit logging: retention window asked: 7 years preferred for some regulated customers; need to confirm Redwood's ability to ship logs to their SIEM.
- KMS: want customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) with HSM-backed key material and ability to rotate keys. Currently evaluating our KMS integration pattern: customer KMS passthrough vs. customer key import.

Technical requirements / priorities:
- Deployment: Private VPC with private control plane, dedicated inference pool for peak trading-window throughput (~500 TPS during batch windows), and burst capacity for end-of-day runs.
- Latency: 30–80ms tail for chat 512-token sequences; throughput target for reranking job ~2000 QPS for batched requests overnight.
- Model preferences: open model family with quantized variants; ability to pin model versions and fallback to smaller variants under capacity pressure.
- Observability: per-route token-level cost breakdown, per-request trace IDs, and ability to export traces to their Datadog/Elastic stack.
- Data controls: request/response redaction, retention controls to delete training data, and per-customer audit trails.

- "We can't hand over KMS control — keys must never leave our KMS." — Head of InfoSec.
- "If you can show a clean SIG/CAIQ mapping and a working KMS passthrough we can move to PO in May." — Procurement lead.
